risk_surfaces: harnessx.Run refactor: fatal-error classification and Parsed==nil default-seeding semantics moved into executeStructured; any reordering regression there changes role fallback behaviour across all Go roles (covered by harnessx tests, but verify no role relied on the old return ordering).

OpenCodeNoInstallPermissionOverlay deny patterns are prefix/exact-string based; overly broad catch-all interaction ('*':'allow' plus specific denies) could be bypassed by equivalent commands not enumerated (uv sync, cargo, cmake fetch, curl-installed toolchains) or could over-deny legitimate paths matching */.worktrees/*/.venv/bin/*.

commitScoped changes delivery semantics: files touched by the coder but missing from the allowed list (including untracked new tests) will be silently left uncommitted, potentially shipping an incomplete fix that still passes targeted tests.
DAG saveCheckpoint insertion changes checkpoint timing/frequency; confirm idempotency and no note/state races with concurrent issue execution.
orch resolve now compares against remoteBranchSHA read before the agent run; stale or missing remote refs could misclassify push success/failure.

Shadow decision resolver adds a harness call (model/provider, 6 turns, timeout 20s) on every ask_user pause — added latency/cost and a new failure surface, though failures fall through to HAX by design.

OpenClaw HITL fallback is env-gated but, once enabled, changes the human-interaction path for approvals; request IDs are process-local and lose uniqueness across worker restarts (mitigated by atomic sequence only within a process lifetime).
Prompt changes are mirrored in Go, Python, and golden testdata; drift between the three copies would break golden tests or cause divergent role behaviour.
PLAN.md now mixes current L3 checkpoints with legacy IN PROGRESS batches; stale readers could act on superseded gates.
pr_narrative: This change hardens SWE-AF's autonomous L3 pipeline along four fronts. First, runtime enforcement: coder, reviewer, and verifier now share one OpenCode permission overlay (harnessx.OpenCodeNoInstallPermissionOverlay) that denies dependency installation and cross-worktree virtualenv execution while allowing normal read/test/build commands; role tests assert the shared constant instead of duplicating JSON, and live canaries confirmed selective fail-closed behaviour on the real FCM path. Second, structured-output robustness: harnessx.Run becomes a thin seam over a centralized executeStructured policy (weak-model recovery, default seeding, nil-slice normalization, fatal-error classification ordering) with an explicit per-role SchemaMode override for narrow roles where incremental whole-file editing is unreliable. Third, delivery integrity: issue builds gain commitScoped delivery that stages only allowed paths, detects unexpected worktree paths, and filters bytecode junk, so temporary diagnostics can no longer become deliverables; the DAG executor also checkpoints completed/failed/skipped barriers before downstream gates to prevent duplicate work on resume. Fourth, HITL evolution: an opt-in OpenClaw fallback replaces HAX when configured via SWE_OPENCLAW_HITL, emitting bounded, secret-free governor.pending/resolved notes; and a shadow-mode pre-HITL Decision Resolver (DecisionCase) produces advisory recommendations that never bypass the human pause. Supporting changes: provider config additions (fcm, gonka), remote-branch snapshot before PR resolution for reliable push detection, coder/reviewer/verifier prompt hardening mirrored across Go and Python with updated golden testdata, PLAN.md L3-19/20/21 checkpoints, and a strict direct-schema regression test for run_qa_synthesizer. Go-side checks (vet, full test suite, targeted role tests) pass; Python-side tests require a runner provisioned without violating the no-install contract.
intent_gaps: L3 gate remains OPEN: no fresh same-case trajectory has yet reached repair -> verifier -> delivery and independent operator acceptance on a delivered exact SHA; this delta alone does not satisfy the semantic acceptance order.

Python-side validation is unproven in this environment: pytest is unavailable and installing it is forbidden for this lane, so tests/test_ask_user.py and tests/test_qa_synthesizer_direct_schema.py have no PASS evidence from here.

Runtime permission overlay is proven by canaries only against the specific deny patterns exercised (pip install, sibling-worktree .venv, plain python allow); no exhaustive pattern-coverage or bypass (e.g. curl|sh, cargo add, poetry) audit exists.
Model adherence (coder/reviewer respecting no-install and stop-after-first-blocker rules) is a separate gate from enforcement and is not closed by this delta.
The exact OpenCode argv / provider provenance for prior L3 runs was only recovered for l3-20/21; earlier historical checkpoint evidence remains uncorroborated.
OpenClaw HITL fallback and the shadow decision resolver have no end-to-end runtime evidence (no real Agent.Pause / cron-bridge execution recorded).
tests/test_qa_synthesizer_direct_schema.py is untracked; if not added before delivery, scoped commit logic may exclude it and the regression coverage would be lost.
